# Build and validation report

The package was generated and exercised against the uploaded PhiUSIIL CSV in this environment.

## Dataset audit
- Raw dataset: 235,795 rows × 56 columns
- Cleaned unique-URL dataset: 235,370 rows
- Duplicate URLs in raw data: 425
- Balanced sample used for each training run: 10,000 rows
- Train/test split: 8,000 / 2,000, stratified

## Model experiments generated by this package
| Experiment | Features | Accuracy | Confusion matrix (labels [0, 1]) |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| V2, HTTPS included | 22 | 98.90% | [[992, 8], [14, 986]] |
| V3, HTTPS excluded | 21 | 96.95% | [[970, 30], [31, 969]] |

V3 is the default inference model. The earlier chat experiments used a different feature schema, so their 99.15% and 97.45% results are not the results of this updated package.

## Manual / external requirement
Day 11's requested 20-case independent benchmark is **not pre-filled**. It requires 10 independently verified phishing URLs and 10 independently verified legitimate URLs with source/provenance notes. The package intentionally does not invent or distribute live malicious URLs.

## Important limitations
- The label mapping 0=phishing and 1=legitimate is the project's working assumption and must be checked against the dataset documentation.
- Dataset holdout metrics do not prove performance on current real-world URLs.
- The extractor's definitions are consistent within this project but do not claim to reproduce the dataset's undocumented feature formulas.
- Random Forest class scores are vote proportions, not calibrated real-world probabilities.
